scope_note: Top-level class for anything independently identifiable in the system.
notes: Do not use directly when a narrower class applies.

scope_note: Actor capable of creating, using, owning, regulating, or influencing entities.
Commercial establishment or enterprise.
Family, household, lineage, or domestic unit.
examples: household maintaining a manuscript recipe book

scope_note: Government agency, ministry, municipality, regulator, or public institution.
Corporate, institutional, association, or collective agent.
Individual person.
Scholarly or technical analysis performed on evidence.
examples: residue analysis; price analysis; provenance assessment

scope_note: Biological or naturally occurring entity relevant to food history.
Named breed, strain, or domesticated population.
Named cultivated plant variety or landrace.
Defined fermentation culture, starter, or microbial community.
Species or other taxonomic unit.
Brand identity, mark, or branded family distinct from one product or manufacturer.
Explicit proposition about history that can be supported, contradicted, or unresolved.
Curated or naturally associated aggregation of items.
Abstract culinary or food-related concept.
Drink concept independent of any one recipe, batch, or branded product.
Named dietary pattern, regimen, or customary intake pattern.
Named or unnamed prepared-food concept independent of any one recipe or serving.
Edible raw material, processed ingredient, additive, or culinary material.
Abstract structure of eating or service.
Transformation, preparation, preservation, service, or consumption process.
Defined method or formula for producing a food or beverage.
examples: household recipe; restaurant formula; industrial formula
notes: May have versions and source occurrences.

scope_note: Shared culinary system, practice, repertoire, or tradition.
examples: Cajun cuisine; tea ceremony; tapas culture

scope_note: Historical or modern measure, serving unit, grade, or portion concept.
Born-digital or digitized resource treated as a discrete object.
Item whose primary role is recorded information.
Bounded occurrence in time involving agents, places, objects, concepts, or activities.
Inspection, certification, licensing, recall, seizure, court action, enactment, etc.
Meal, festival, banquet, fair, competition, ceremony, or social event.
Specific harvest, batch, manufacture, cooking, bottling, or processing event.
Specific act or occasion of serving, purchasing, or consuming food.
Sale, auction, donation, trade, consignment, or ownership transfer.
Version, translation, revision, performance, or textual expression of a work.
External or internal identity used for reconciliation.
examples: VIAF ID; Getty AAT ID; catalogue number

scope_note: Specific physical or digital exemplar.
examples: signed cookbook copy; one printed menu

scope_note: Published or produced embodiment shared by multiple copies.
Photographic, audio, moving-image, or graphic item.
Human-made tangible object whose primary role is not merely carrying text.
Structured observation that something appeared, existed, was served, sold, produced, or mentioned at a given time/place/source.
Geographic, built, or functional location.
Country, region, city, neighborhood, landscape, body of water, etc.
examples: Burgundy; New Orleans; Gulf of Maine

scope_note: Specific physical site or structure.
examples: restaurant building; farm; market hall; archaeological site

scope_note: Commercially defined marketed product, distinct from a generic food concept.
Sustained organized activity or initiative that is more persistent than a single event.
examples: advertising campaign; school-lunch program; rationing scheme; nutrition campaign
notes: Use Event for discrete occurrences; use Program for an ongoing organized activity.

scope_note: Bibliographic, archival, oral, digital, or material source used as evidence.
examples: book page; newspaper issue; archival folder

scope_note: Biological, chemical, archaeological, or reference specimen.
Abstract intellectual or creative creation.
